name: orreth
description: Identity-anchored memory for AI agent universes — permanent identities (Ed25519/DID), signed append-only memory, governed retrieval, one Rust binary. Demo: demo.orreth.ai · Docs: docs.orreth.ai

paragraphs: A kernel for fleets of agents. Identity, memory, rails, meter, gate, watches and levers are held by the kernel; policy is held by humans; an intention is the unit of control. Everything a body does lands on one signed record, and a person can always stop what the machine manages.
THE PANEL on a running kernel: geometry is what is declared, light is what is happening, colour is who did it. Walk it yourself at demo.orreth.ai; the architecture is drawn in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

The systemic problem in agent fleets today is entropy. Every agent brings its own identity story, its own memory, its own way of calling a tool, its own idea of what it may do and what it costs; put twenty of them on one problem and nobody can say who did what, under which law, for how much, or how to stop it. Frameworks add loops; they do not remove the entropy.
features: Identity — a keypair is a self, and a self survives the process. A body re-joins as the same
Memory — one signed, append-only record on the ground; corrections are siblings, never
Rails — every ask, reply, fact and tool call rides the same envelope over the same rails
Meter — every thought a body has goes through one gateway under the body's own key, and
Gate — a body joins through a five-status desk; a person's word is the only thing that admits
